sections.h2: Choosing how to sell in Lufkin
sections.html:
You can use an agent, sell by yourself, or find a cash buyer who is unbothered by the repair list. Listing may fetch the best price; cash trades some price for speed and certainty.

Lufkin is the Angelina County seat, at the crossing of U.S. highways 59 and 69 in the East Texas Piney Woods. The buyer pool is local and tied to timber, manufacturing and health care. A house needing work will find a buyer, though often after a longer stay on the market, so plan the asking price around that.

  • Listing: best for a move-in-ready house when you can handle showings and an appraisal.
  • Private sale: you keep the commission and run the contract yourself.
  • Cash offer: suits repairs, liens, an estate or a tenant you would rather not manage.

sections.h2: Older houses and what buyers check
sections.html:
The oldest blocks in Lufkin sit near the rail core, with later subdivisions spreading outward. Many older houses date to the decades when timber and manufacturing grew the town, and a buyer may ask when major systems were last replaced. Before a lender backs a conventional buyer, an older house may need work on its roof, wiring or foundation.

A mix of industry, services and recreation, from Sam Rayburn Reservoir to hunting land, means buyers arrive from several directions. Jobs in manufacturing and oilfield equipment rise and fall with the industry, so sell when you need to rather than waiting for a peak. Point school-minded buyers to the Lufkin Independent School District itself for its current campuses.

sections.h2: Who appraises and bills Lufkin property
sections.html:
The Angelina County Appraisal District values property throughout the county each January 1 and passes the values to the taxing units. Among the units it serves are the City of Lufkin, Angelina County, Angelina College and Lufkin ISD, plus several other school districts and two water districts.

The district keeps ownership records, assigns market value, administers exemptions and special appraisal, and explains disputes and appeals. Its outreach number is (936) 634-8456.

Most Lufkin homes are billed by the city, county, college and Lufkin ISD; a parcel outside the city limits skips the city line. Your bill shows which units apply.

sections.h2: Tax dates for a Lufkin owner
sections.html:
Taxing units on a typical Lufkin bill
Taxing unitAppears on your bill when
City of LufkinThe parcel is inside city limits
Angelina CountyAlways, for land in the county
Angelina CollegeAlways, for land in the district
Lufkin ISDThe house is in that school district

Values are fixed each January 1, which is also when the lien attaches. Mid-May is protest time, bills arrive near October 1, and the end of January is the payment deadline. On February 1 an unpaid balance gets a 6 percent penalty and starts collecting 1 percent monthly interest.

At closing the agent splits the year's tax between you and the buyer. A lender or buyer who asks for a tax certificate can get one from the Angelina County tax office.

• Every school district takes $140,000 off a homestead, and seniors and disabled owners get $60,000 beyond that.
  • For a qualifying senior or disabled homeowner, a ceiling can freeze the school tax at the amount owed in the first year they qualified.
  • After the first exemption year, a homestead's value can climb by no more than 10 percent annually.
  • A disabled veteran gets tiered exemptions, with a total exemption for a 100 percent rating.

The exemptions belong to you, not the house, so the buyer files again after closing.

sections.h2: If a Lufkin mortgage payment slips
sections.html:
Move early. A borrower with a Texas deed of trust has twenty days from the default notice to reinstate, and three weeks must pass between the sale notice and the auction. Auctions are open to the public once a month, during the day.

Foreclosure usually cannot begin under federal rules until a home loan is over 120 days behind. After a foreclosure sale, leftover money goes first to junior lienholders and then to the former owner, and any suit over a shortfall has a two-year limit.

A sale beforehand lets you choose the buyer, skip the foreclosure record and keep your equity. Ask the servicer for a written payoff.

Title comes first. A will can be probated until four years after the death. A muniment of title lets heirs act on the will. If there is none, a small estate affidavit can cover assets below a set dollar ceiling, and the homestead does not count toward it.

When a renter lives there, the landlord typically sends three days' written notice, files in justice court, and can ask for a writ of possession six days after judgment. Many owners avoid all that by selling with the renter in place. Before signing, confirm with the appraisal district who the owner of record is.

Land in the county is recorded by the Angelina County Clerk, once a notary or similar officer has acknowledged the signature. Recording costs $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, plus capped records fees, under the state clerk manual. The closing agent usually files and deducts the cost.

Selling slowly in Lufkin is not unusual for a house that needs work. If you can wait, make the small fixes that buyers notice first: a clean exterior, working systems and a tidy yard. If you cannot wait, a cash offer gives you a date. Neither answer is wrong. What matters is that you know what each path leaves you after the mortgage, the tax share and recording costs.

Ask the appraisal district for the year's assessed value so you know what the house is carried at, and ask the tax office for the amount due. A buyer's lender will want both figures, and having them in hand keeps the contract from stalling in its first week.

sections.h2: Lufkin buyers and where they come from
sections.html: Local employers in timber, manufacturing, paper and health care supply many of the buyers for Lufkin houses, and the area's lakes and hunting land bring in others. A seller who knows which group fits the house can aim the listing: a family house near the older core appeals to someone who wants an established neighborhood, while a worn house on a big lot may suit an investor. State the lot size, the age of the roof and the condition of the plumbing in plain terms, and say whether the house sits inside the city limits so buyers know which tax bill to expect.

After you accept an offer, the closing agent asks your lender for the payoff, requests a tax certificate from the Angelina County tax office, drafts the deed and schedules the signing. After you sign before a notary, the agent files the deed with the county clerk and pays the recording charge from your proceeds. You receive the balance. If the buyer needs a homestead exemption, they apply to the appraisal district themselves.

Keep every document the agent sends. If a question about the tax split comes up later, the closing statement is the record.

Collect the deed, your latest Angelina County tax bill, a loan payoff statement and any repair receipts. Call the appraisal district and ask which exemptions are active and whose name they are under. Ask the tax office what is owed today. If you have a tenant, write down the lease terms.

Then ask two or three cash buyers and one listing agent for numbers. A written offer should show the price, the closing date and who pays title and recording costs. Subtract your payoff and tax share from each to see what you actually keep.

faqs.a: Angelina County, where Lufkin is the seat. Both the appraisal district and the clerk's office are in Angelina County.

faqs.q: Can a Lufkin house sell as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Investors buy in present condition and discount the price for repairs and holding time. Compare that with a listing price.

faqs.q: When do Lufkin property taxes turn late?
faqs.a: Most unpaid Texas taxes are delinquent on February 1. Penalty (six percent) and interest (one percent) begin then, and by July 1 the penalty is 12 percent.

faqs.q: Is probate required before selling an inherited Lufkin house?
faqs.a: Usually some court or recorded step must show ownership. Heirs can prove ownership through a probated will, a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit, or a transfer on death deed that the owner recorded earlier.

faqs.q: How long does Texas foreclosure take after a default notice?
faqs.a: Twenty days to cure after the default notice, then a sale notice three weeks before the monthly auction. Selling earlier can protect equity.
